![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266392/assets/e2ed2c96d7bcc3b00d8e00d754b9e8b2492e15df6bd568c06e9d25a9ce658a58.png)

An experiment consists of taking $14$ measurements of rainfall (in $\text{mm}$) during the rainy season in Africa. The results are presented above in the form of a histogram. Assuming that the rainfall measurements within each class interval are uniformly distributed, find an estimate of the mean rainfall, rounded to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, the mean can be estimated as follows:

$$
\overset{―}{x}≈\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{K}{f}_{i}\cdot {m}_{i}
$$

where

- ${f}_{i}$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

- ${m}_{i}$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class, and

- $n$ is the total number of observations.

To estimate the mean, we represent the given data as a table and add columns for the midpoints of each class and the products of the midpoints and frequencies.

| Rainfall ($\text{mm}$) | ${m}_{i}$ | ${f}_{i}$ | ${m}_{i}\cdot {f}_{i}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $200\le r<250$ | $225$ | $3$ | $675$ |
| $250\le r<300$ | $275$ | $5$ | $1375$ |
| $300\le r<350$ | $325$ | $4$ | $1300$ |
| $350\le r<400$ | $375$ | $2$ | $750$ |

$$

$$

Finally, we sum the values in the last column and divide by $14$ (the total number of observations).

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{r} & ≈\frac{675+1375+1300+750}{14} \\  & =\frac{4100}{14} \\  & ≈292.86\,\text{mm}\end{aligned}
$$
